title_en: The Martyrdom of Justin and His Companions
author: Unknown (Acts of the Martyrs)
occasion: An account of the arrest, interrogation, and execution of Justin and five companions in Rome under the prefect Rusticus. The text narrates their confession, condemnation, beheading, and the secret burial of their bodies by believers.
argument: Justin and five companions are brought before the prefect Rusticus for refusing to sacrifice to the gods. Justin explains that he follows the true teaching of the Christians, worshipping the God of the Christians, the one maker of all creation, and his Child Jesus Christ, whose coming the prophets foretold. Each companion confesses himself a Christian; Paeon and Euelpistus say they received the faith from their parents, while Hierax names Christ as his true father. When threatened with scourging and beheading, they refuse to sacrifice, declaring their hope of salvation and boldness before the judgment seat of Christ. Rusticus condemns them to be scourged and beheaded, and they are executed, after which believers secretly bury their bodies.

outline.move: The martyrs are arrested and brought before the prefect Rusticus, who questions Justin about his beliefs; Justin confesses the God of the Christians and Jesus Christ as God's Child.
Rusticus asks where Christians assemble; Justin says God is not confined to a place, states he stays above the bath of Martinus son of Timiotinus, and affirms he is a Christian.
Rusticus questions each companion, and all confess themselves Christians; Paeon and Euelpistus cite their parents, while Hierax names Christ as his true father.
Rusticus threatens Justin and the others with death unless they sacrifice; they refuse and express hope of salvation and boldness before Christ's judgment seat.
Rusticus sentences them to scourging and beheading; they are executed and their bodies buried secretly by believers.

cast.name: Justin

cast.name: Rusticus
cast.who: Prefect of Rome who interrogates and condemns the martyrs.

cast.name: Chariton
cast.who: One of the companions who confesses himself a Christian.

cast.name: Charito
cast.who: A woman among the companions who confesses herself a Christian.

cast.name: Euelpistus
cast.who: A slave of Caesar from Cappadocia who confesses himself a Christian.

cast.name: Hierax
cast.who: A companion from Iconium in Phrygia who confesses himself a Christian and names Christ as his true father.

cast.name: Paeon
cast.who: A companion who received the Christian confession from his parents.

cast.name: Liberianus
cast.who: A companion who confesses himself a Christian and worships the one true God.

scripture: The text does not quote Scripture directly, but refers to the prophets who foretold Christ's coming. No LXX/Vulgate book names or Psalm numbering are used.
uncertain: The exact date of the martyrdom; the text does not specify a year.
The identity of the author; the text is anonymous.
The precise location of the bath of Martinus son of Timiotinus.
Whether the section divisions correspond to original manuscript divisions or were added later.
The intended addressee; the text does not state one.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Χαριτοῦς as source form for Charito
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ΜΑΡΤΥΡΙΟΝ ΤΩΝ ΑΓΙΩΝ ΜΑΡΤΥΡΩΝ ΙΟΥΣΤΙΝΟΥ ΧΑΡΙΤΩΝΟΣ, ΧΑΡΙΤΟΥΣ, ΠΑΙΩΝΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΛΙΒΕΡΙΑΝΟΥ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Χαρίτωνος (genitive of Χαρίτων) is the source form in the title; Χαριτοῦς is a genitive form. The nominative should be Χαριτώ.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Euelpistus is 'a slave of Caesar from Cappadocia'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Εὐέλπιστος, δοῦλος Καίσαρος, ἀπεκρίνατο· Κἀγὼ Χριστιανός εἰμι ἐλευθερωθεὶς ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Euelpistus identifies himself as 'δοῦλος Καίσαρος' (slave of Caesar) but does not say he is from Cappadocia; his parents are in Cappadocia (Ἐν τῇ Καππαδοκίᾳ). He may be from elsewhere.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Καὶ ἐγὼ, ἀπὸ Ἰκονίου τῆς Φρυγίας ἀποσπασθείς, ἐνθάδε ἐλήλυθα
_unresolved_facts.fix: Hierax says he was 'torn away from/apart from Iconium of Phrygia' (ἀποσπασθείς), not that he is from there. The phrasing suggests he was separated from there, not necessarily that it was his origin.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ῥουστικὸς τῷ Ἱέρακι λέγει· Οἱ σοὶ γονεῖς ποῦ εἰσίν; ὁ δὲ ἀπεκρίνατο λέγων· Ὁ ἀληθινὸς ἡμῶν πατήρ ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός
_unresolved_facts.fix: The phrase 'ὁ δὲ ἀπεκρίνατο' refers to Hierax but is not a standard introduction marking his voice; it's a narrative continuation. The actual speaker introduction is implicit through the dialogue structure.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Παῖς Θεοῦ rendered as 'Child of God'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Καὶ Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν, Παῖδα Θεοῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Παῖς Θεοῦ means 'Servant of God' or 'Son of God' (the latter confirmed by Θεοῦ Υἱός later); 'Child of God' is anachronistic and theologically imprecise for this context. The brief's own names entry has 'Son of God' for Θεοῦ Υἱός but should note Παῖς Θεοῦ as 'Servant of God' or 'Son of God'.
